citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot, Loic Landrieu (2021). Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV 2021.
creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot, Loic Landrieu (LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN)
description: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series) is the first large-scale, publicly available Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations for agricultural parcel mapping. It comprises 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral Sentinel-2 images (10 spectral bands, 128×128 pixels at 10m resolution) covering over 4,000 km² across four regions of France, with over 2 billion annotated pixels and 124,422 individualized parcels labeled with 18 crop types plus background.
name: PASTIS-HD
publisher: IGNF (Institut national de l'information géographique et forestière)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98%, and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were derived from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). Each pixel was annotated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each unique parcel received a unique instance label. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch extent were annotated with the void label. The FLPIS 73-class nomenclature was reduced to 18 classes by selecting classes with at least 400 parcels and samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common crop classes. To mitigate this, patches were selected favoring those with rare crop types. The dataset covers only four regions of France, which may not represent all climates and crop distributions globally. Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover, which introduces noise in the data.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were collected from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform via THEIA (value-added data processed by CNES for the Theia data cluster using Copernicus data). Images were taken from 4 different Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of the French metropolitan territory, covering a wide variety of climates and crop distributions. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations with a median time between acquisitions of 5 days. Annotations were derived from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered by the Sentinel data provider THEIA and not included. Even after this filtering, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover (approximately 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover). The authors opted not to apply further preprocessing or cloud detection, leaving the raw data as-is to encourage methods that can handle such acquisitions. Temporal sampling is irregular, with sequences containing between 33 and 61 acquisitions depending on location.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of Sentinel-2 multi-spectral satellite imagery with 13 spectral bands at 10m spatial resolution, obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform (scihub.copernicus.eu). Annotation source data is the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN, which uses a 73-class breakdown for crop types as reported by farmers.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: All-zeroes images are appended at the end of shorter sequences to match the length of the longer sequence in a batch (zero-padding). A padding mask is retained to prevent spatial and temporal encoding of padded values and to exclude them from temporal averages.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to four regions of France and may not generalize to other geographic areas or crop systems. The dataset is highly class-imbalanced (ratio over 50 between most and least common classes). Approximately 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. The temporal sampling is irregular due to cloud filtering and satellite orbit schedules. The dataset covers only 18 crop types out of the 73 in the FLPIS nomenclature.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split into 5 folds for cross-validation, with a 1 km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination. Folds were chosen with comparable class distributions (measured by pairwise Kullback-Leibler divergence) and each fold contains patches from all four Sentinel tiles. Adjacent patches were prevented from being in different folds to avoid data contamination.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Atmospheric correction and resampling to 10 meters per pixel were applied to Sentinel-2 images. Atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10 were removed, retaining 10 spectral bands. Sentinel tiles were subdivided into 128×128 pixel patches (1.28×1.28 km). 2,433 patches were selected from ~24,000 available patches (10%), favoring patches with rare crop types to decrease extreme class imbalance. Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered by the Sentinel data provider and not included.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. The dataset supports applications with major financial and environmental stakes, including crop mapping, urban development surveying, and deforestation monitoring.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on Satellite Image Time Series (SITS); semantic segmentation of agricultural parcels; crop type mapping; monitoring agricultural subsidies allocation; ensuring crop rotation practices; surveying urban development and deforestation; Earth observation research.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Annotations are derived from the FLPIS administrative database, not from multiple independent annotators; no per-item annotation count is discussed.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are derived from the French LPIS administrative database (as reported by farmers), not from human annotators with described demographics.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Annotations are derived from the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS), an administrative database, not a crowdsourcing or annotation platform.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools are described for the dataset creation; annotations come from the administrative FLPIS database.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains satellite imagery and agricultural parcel annotations; no personal or sensitive information about individuals is collected or discussed.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
